rv.q: The marvel of Ms. Merkerson’s performance in this revitalizing production of a play often dismissed as a soggy period piece is how completely and starkly she allows us to see what Lola sees.
Come Back, Little Sheba doesn't leap into the present tense: Yesterday's play of the year has become a movie of the week.
It is unlikely that anyone can make this obvious old soaper hold the stage today.
His writing, although moving, doesn’t hold up well, and Pressman’s tidy production seems to accentuate the flaws rather than conceal them.

cn.t: Merkerson earns praise for her deeply felt, heart-stopping performance, but Inge's 1950 drama feels decidedly dated and tame to most critics, resulting in mixed reception for this earnest revival.

vs.sum: The Samuel J. Friedman Theatre offers good sightlines with minimal obstructions and a well-raked mezzanine, ensuring a clear view from most seats. The sound quality is consistently praised, and the seating is comfortable with decent legroom. The theater's ambiance is enhanced by its elegant design following renovation, though facilities like restrooms are average, leading to some congestion during intermissions.

acc.note: Elevator to all levels. Built-in induction loop for t-coil hearing aids.
